title: Cost & ROI Analysis — Model Routing and Economic Gaps (2026-05-03)
summary: Model tier routing is architecturally correct with cost-optimized per-persona assignment. Batch mission parallelism (the highest cost-saving mechanism) is stubbed. Supabase billing table is unreachable, blocking ROI report generation. Estimated cost per canonical 8-step mission: $0.08–$0.42 depending on task complexity.
key_findings: selectTierByComplexity() in crew-manifest.ts correctly routes: score < 0.3 → HAIKU, < 0.7 → SONNET, >= 0.7 → OPUS
enrichAgentsWithPersonas() in HTTP bridge enforces cost routing before Python CrewAI invocation — no LLM calls use wrong tier
runMissions batch concurrency is a stub — sequential fallback only, parallelism cost savings are not realized
generate_roi_report tool exists but Supabase billing table unreachable — ROI data unavailable
v11 reflection loop adds up to 3x execution cost per mission if quality gate fails — budget headroom must account for worst case
Counselor Troi's explicit role is cost-optimization validation (Step 2 of canonical flow) — she gates budget before expensive SONNET/OPUS steps run
BarItalia STL target: under $1.50 per full 8-step mission — achievable with current tier routing if Picard (OPUS) is constrained to planning only
cost_optimization_recommendations: Implement runMissions with concurrency limit of 3-5 to enable parallel persona execution (reduces wall-clock time without increasing cost)
Add Counselor Troi budget gate as a hard check — abort mission if projected cost exceeds budget constraint
Restore Supabase connection to enable billing table writes and ROI report generation
Consider downgrading captain_picard from OPUS to SONNET for non-strategic missions — saves $14.75/M tokens
Enable MODEL_CREW_MANAGER env override in .env to allow operators to dial Picard's model without code changes
